items.title: Mist
items.note: Patrick Higgins on guitar and percussion, with Nicolás Jaar processing it live, recorded over three years in Berlin and upstate New York. The review describes sparse textures and metallic percussion where melodies surface and dissolve, and Judith Hamann's cello appears on some tracks.

items.artist: Sylvia Meyer & Lila Tirando a Violeta
items.title: Doble Ceniza
items.note: A dreamy, mostly beatless collaboration on pop soil. Lila's Latin-tinged machine music sits against Meyer's austere piano and voice.

items.title: All Ages
items.note: His first album in six years, and his first for Warp. It draws on the hardcore punk shows he grew up with, and the review half-jokingly calls it his midlife crisis record.

items.title: Bright Folk
items.note: Third album from the Mongolian pianist and her quartet, on Motéma. It's built around the idea of home as a feeling you carry with you, and her debut Rising Sun was a poised record that makes this worth following up.

items.title: Whispers
items.note: Her first release since the surprise album Lifetime, co-produced with Eurohead. It's a standalone single for now.

items.title: East Side Love Story
items.note: A debut of intimate love songs, with rich vocals and production that sounds true to an older era. Bandcamp Daily called it a standout.

items.title: Interastral Communications
items.note: A debut that imagines The Orb's space ambient pushed decades forward, through breakbeat and IDM. Looped flute, choral voices and fast drums, and it ends in a whisper.

items.title: Mesopotamian #1
items.note: Self-released debut EP from a Lebanese artist based in Brooklyn, written as a tribute to her homeland. Small and easy to miss, which is why it's here.

items.title: Khudgarzi
items.note: The singer sets Indian musical traditions against atmospheric electronics. The songs push back against the limits put on women.

items.title: With Child, Without
items.note: A sorrowful album about pregnancy loss, infertility and IVF. The review says her later birth doesn't soften the grief, and that honesty is the reason to hear it.

items.title: NOON
items.note: The Quietus made this their album of the week. It pairs the Lancashire composer with the Room40 boss, and the review says the two find "a still point in the midst of the storm of contemporary history".
items.source: Juno Ambient / Drone / Experimental (via The Quietus)

items.title: 711Falx
items.note: A debut album and the first release on Fovea Specs. Bandcamp Daily heard dubby chord stabs and crinkly pads with a sneaky sense of motion, and the label notes nods to 2-step and footwork along the way.
items.source: Juno Ambient / Drone / Experimental (via Bandcamp Daily)

items.artist: Sylvia Meyer & Lila Tirando a Violeta
items.title: Doble Ceniza
items.note: A five-track EP where two Uruguayan artists from different generations meet. Sylvia Meyer's old piano and voice demos are reshaped with field recordings and fragments, and Bandcamp Daily called it a blissful, mostly beatless listen.

items.title: Khudgarzi
items.note: Her first full album, on Erased Tapes, sung mostly in Urdu over Hindustani, Carnatic, Turkish and Arabic instruments. Bandcamp Daily says it filters traditional currents into futuristic electronic landscapes, like her mentor Arooj Aftab with a bit more bite.

items.title: MO LÉAN (Expanded)
items.note: An expanded international edition, via Domino, of her 2024 album, so not strictly new, but worth it. She reworks the Irish funeral lament with electronics, and Bandcamp Daily points to the trip-hop of "Cití" and the ambient-to-dub drift of "Oh Lovely Appearance of Death".

items.title: All Ages
items.note: A new album for Warp. The Quietus interviewed him about the skateboarding and hardcore scenes that shaped him as a teenager, and the rebellion against himself that went into making it.

items.title: East Side Love Story
items.note: A debut made over six years in East LA and co-produced with Chris McClenney, drawing on Chicano soul, Motown and G-funk. Bandcamp Daily called it one of the year's most swoon-worthy debuts.

items.title: Diana
items.note: A guitar quartet record on ECM. Jazz Views called it a marvellous set of original compositions that pull at the ears and the heart.

items.title: Riders of the Setting Sun
items.note: The band leave their black metal past behind for gothic Americana built on acoustic guitar, slide and memorable melodies. David Eugene Edwards and Jay Munly guest, according to Bandcamp Daily's album of the day write-up.

items.title: On Course But No-One There To Salute You
items.note: Partly recorded at 4AD's studios. I could only read The Quietus feed summary, which calls it "less sunburst and snowblind than wind-battered and rain-sodden", so give it a listen before you buy.
items.source: Juno Ambient / Drone / Experimental (via The Quietus)

items.title: No Human Tongue Can Tell
items.note: The Lankum singer's first solo album is a set of traditional folk songs, made with John Spud Murphy and partly inspired by Tubular Bells. Pitchfork gave it 8.0, and it's the best-reviewed record here. Out Nov 13 on Rough Trade.

items.title: Keep Driving, Son
items.note: The Danish composer writes for five Copenhagen voices, including ML Buch and Ydegirl, telling the story of two men who knew the same woman. Picked for Pitchfork Selects on Nov 17. Out Nov 16.

items.title: Live at the Barbican
items.note: Recorded at her sold-out Barbican show in March 2025, where she played Nobody Loves You More with a 25-piece ensemble. Pitchfork gave it 7.7. Out Nov 13 on 4AD.

items.title: Dizzy
items.note: His official comeback single goes back to the darker sound of Black City, with snaking riffs, thumping kicks and his low baritone. A Pitchfork Selects pick from Nov 17. Out Nov 11.

A new EP from the Cameroonian singer-songwriter, who works across experimental R&B, folk and glitch. Pitchfork put a song from it on Selects this week. There's no Pitchfork review or score yet. Out Nov 19.

items.title: Great Destroyer
items.note: Their first new song since last year's debut album. It starts with soft guitar and builds into a big orchestral post-rock swell. A Pitchfork Selects pick from Nov 17. Out Nov 11.

items.title: Visual Culture of Northeast Brazil (Cordel Edition)
items.note: A 700-page study of cordel, the cheap pamphlet poetry of Brazil's Northeast with its woodcut covers. Victor Yves treats it as a communication system rather than folklore, with essays, close visual analysis, interviews and an anthology of more than 500 illustrations. It grew out of his CASCA Archive of Northeast Brazilian design, and comes as a small, thick, thread-sewn hardcover. Draw Down has it in stock too.

items.title: The Century of the Poster: Slovenian Poster Design in the 20th Century
items.note: More than 300 Slovenian posters, drawn from the visual communications collection at the Museum of Architecture and Design in Ljubljana and from libraries, archives and private holdings. It runs from early 20th century lithographs through modernism to post-socialist work, and reads the poster as a tool that shaped public space and political debate. 390 pages, paperback, in English. This week's poster book.

items.title: MXTP Vol. 2 (Music Typefaces)
items.note: The second font mixtape from Maxitype, the independent Swiss foundry and publisher. The typefaces came out of a summer type residency, and all of them are made for or inspired by music, from grunge and jungle to classical and Goa trance. 176 pages, hardcover, with a download code for 46 typefaces, so it is half specimen and half font library.

items.title: Bilingual Typography: A Guide to Categorisation and Design Principles
items.note: A small guide to setting two languages in one layout, built on Khajeh's doctoral research into Arabic and Latin typography and her own bilingual design work. It defines key terms, proposes new categories for bilingual layouts and sets out principles for balancing them. 144 pages, hardcover with a round spine, spot colours on uncoated paper. Ships in January 2027.

items.title: Design Subject to Change: Human Agency in the Digital Interface
items.note: Part manifesto and part confession from an interface designer who has spent a decade building software at scale. Spradlin asks why so many digital products now work against the people using them, drawing on design history, social theory and philosophy, and argues that the future of the interface is still open. Edited by Jarrett Fuller, with a foreword by Silvio Lorusso and a cover by Oliver Munday. 280 pages, expected mid to late January 2027.

items.title: The World's Best Typography: Typography 47
items.note: The latest Type Directors Club winners in communication design, lettering and typeface design, now published by Slanted. This edition is smaller and cheaper than before, with a Judges' Choices section where jurors explain their picks and an index of typefaces and designers. 384 pages, edited by Griffin McCabe and Joe Newton, art directed by Lars Harmsen and Marian Misiak.

items.title: The Best Dutch Book Designs 2025
items.note: The yearly round-up of the best designed Dutch books, presented by the Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam. Two juries pick the books, one of design, publishing and production people and one of graphic design students, and they look at typography, image editing, paper, printing and binding. 332 pages, Dutch and English. A good catalogue to steal ideas from.

items.title: To Have an Idea: 50 Years of Idea Books
items.note: Idea Books has distributed art, architecture and design books out of Amsterdam since 1976, and this is its 50th birthday book. Current and former staff, reps, publishers and customers share stories, next to archive documents, behind-the-scenes material and favourite titles. 156 pages, designed by Dongyoung Lee with photographs by Johannes Schwartz. A look at the part of the book world readers rarely see.

items.title: Mikhail Lychkovskiy
items.note: Poster designer who builds his work on type and grids, with Müller-Brockmann, Ruder and Hofmann as touchstones and French posters as a newer interest. He mostly works in Figma but also makes posters by hand with metal and wood type, paint and brushes, a habit he picked up from Peter Bankov. This spring he had a solo show, Typoposterized, at PANDA Platforma in Berlin, with a screen printed poster that tries to fit in as many ways of handling type as possible.

items.title: Thiago Lacaz
items.note: Rio designer who makes posters for Brazilian musicians, films and festivals, plus book covers. His animated poster for a micro bookstore's 11th birthday, with coloured bars that read as both book spines and a sound equalizer, was picked for the Typographic Arts 100 this year. His newest posters, for Amaro Freitas and Romulo Fróes, are on Typographic Posters, and he has won first place at the International Poster Biennial in Mexico.

items.title: Damage Waffle Crew LS, D.Brown
items.note: A cotton waffle crew with distressing built in, so it already looks worn. Relaxed cut with dropped shoulders and a slightly longer body for layering. Made in Japan.

items.title: Chambray Baggy Chino Pants, Beige
items.note: Wide, relaxed chinos with double front pleats that round out through the hip and thigh. The fabric is a dense cotton and poly chambray with a slight sheen. The waist and hem both adjust.

items.title: Dou Trousers, Cotton Denim Sashiko, Black
items.note: Heavy cotton sashiko denim with a stone bio finish to soften it up. Relaxed fit, zip front, an inside drawstring and reinforced double knees. Made in Japan, and no big logos.

items.title: ANCELLM
items.note: A Japanese label started in 2021 by Kazuya Yamachika. Haven says the clothes use natural materials, layered dyeing and hand finishing, and are meant to change as you wear them. Most pieces cost more than £300, but the waffle crews come in well under.

items.title: 10oz Canvas Coverall, Kakishibu Wine
items.note: A chore coat in 10oz Kurashiki canvas, dyed with persimmon tannin to a wine colour that darkens in the sun. It comes pre-washed and has a hand-painted Amakusa pottery stone button. Made in Japan.

items.title: Santa Cruz Black Jeans, Relaxed Tapered
items.note: Black on black 12oz selvedge, woven on shuttle looms at Nihon Menpu. Relaxed through the top with a gentle taper below the knee. Made in Japan, with hand-felled belt loops and single needle stitching.

items.title: Double Face L/S Crewneck, Natural
items.note: A relaxed long sleeve in double faced cotton jersey. Each side has its own texture, and the two layers hold warm air. Made in Japan.

items.title: Double Face Crew Socks, Merino Wool & Organic Cotton, Charcoal
items.note: Merino on the outside and organic cotton next to the skin, in a chunky low gauge knit. Rototo knits them in Koryo, Nara, on a mix of old and new machines. An easy small treat.

items.title: Seuvas
items.note: A canvas clothing label that sews in Kurashiki, Okayama, using canvas from the nearby Takeyari mill, founded in 1888. They work with natural dyers and recycled cotton and wool, and use porcelain buttons made from Amakusa pottery stone. Rivet & Hide has new kakishibu dyed pieces in now.

items.title: 4102 Shaggy Ombre Check Open Collar Shirt, Black
items.note: An open collar shirt in a shaggy ombre check from the Osaka denim maker. It's one of a batch of new Fullcount pieces at Son of a Stag this week.

items.title: 3771 Fading Series Sweatshirt, Black
items.note: Part of Fullcount's Fading series, in plain black with no graphics. Fullcount has been making denim in Osaka since the early nineties, and its sweats are now arriving at Son of a Stag.

items.title: 5222LB Brushed Rib Flat Seam Longsleeve T Shirt, Ecru
items.note: A brushed rib long sleeve with flat seams, in ecru. A good under layer for the colder weeks, and the most affordable of the new Fullcount pieces.

items.title: Lot. 223 10oz Denim Painter Jeans, Raw
items.note: Painter jeans in raw 10oz denim. It's a loose workwear shape, and it costs less than most of the Japanese denim at Son of a Stag.

items.title: 1980s German Army Trainer, Panna Nubuck
items.note: Reproduction of Found started in 2016 and remakes military shoes, going by its own profile. This is their version of the 1980s German army trainer, in panna nubuck.

items.title: Work 5 Pocket Easy Pants, Olive
items.note: Yoko Sakamoto has new stock at both Peggs & Son and Neighbour this season. Most of the range costs well over £300, but these olive easy pants come in just under.

items.title: Stand Collar Jacket, Heather Beige
items.note: A plain stand collar jacket in heather beige from Danton. Peggs & Son has it with Danton's new half coat, hooded jacket and gloves.

items.title: Grandpa Gloves, Mix Brown
items.note: Gloves in a mixed brown from Ends and Means, new in at Peggs & Son. A small, cheap way to add something warm for winter.

items.title: Baggy Straight Pants, Dark Navy
items.note: Goldwin is a Japanese brand with its roots in skiing. These are a roomy straight leg in dark navy, new in at Oi Polloi.

items.title: Everyday Use Sacoche, Dark Brown
items.note: A small everyday shoulder bag in dark brown from Snow Peak, the outdoor company from Niigata. It's useful, low key, and £50.

items.title: 5G Boucle Cardigan, Natural
items.note: A chunky looped boucle cardigan in a melange yarn with faint tonal stripes. It's wide and boxy with a shorter body, and Goodhood says it runs large. It's mostly synthetic with a little wool.
